name: n4_station_health
description: Station health in one call, each section answered on its own: system (the SystemService slots by their station names: CPU usage in percent, memory as the station reports it plus memory_used_percent, version, host, time), points (total, ok, null_only, not_ok_count, a count per status flag in by_flag and the not-ok ones in not_ok, up to max_not_ok; ok is no flag, null_only is the flag null alone, a point with no value and not a fault, and not ok is any other flag, so ok + null_only + not_ok_count = total; proxy is the points whose proxy extension is not control:NullProxyExt, the ones a licence counts), networks and devices (the same, plus disabled and each not-ok entry's name, type and enabled), totals (the n4_inventory totals of the same rows, with rows_truncated when a query feeding them was cut), capacity (resources: the Global Capacity table of the spy metrics page, per resource used and limit, unlimited true where the station shows no limit, and live; recount: its recount times) and elapsed_ms. Two counts sit side by side in a resource: used is the licence's own tally, the number to quote against limit for licensing, and it only grows until a capacity recount or a station restart; live is what the station really holds now (networks, devices and proxy points of the whole station; null for a resource this tool does not count or when base is a subtree). may_be_inflated is true, with an inflation_note, when a used is above its live or the recount has never run. A section that fails is {error} and the others still answer. capacity is null with a capacity_note when the spy metrics page is unreachable or holds no Global Capacity table: never a guessed count. capacity_truncated is true, and capacity_note says so, when the page was cut before it was read whole, so resources may be missing; rows of the table that do not match its header are counted in capacity_note. In a section, truncated means not_ok was cut at max_not_ok (not_ok_count is whole) and rows_truncated means the query hit max_rows, so the counts are lower bounds. A status the station did not answer counts under the flag unknown and as not ok, never as ok. license is the licence manager page (spy sysManagers/licenseManager) in short: licenses (name, expires, valid, with state when not valid, and days_left counted from the station's own date, the day of system.systemTime; null for never, for an expiry that is not a date or when that date is unknown; up to 100, licenses_count when more), nearest_expiry (the earliest dated expiry among licences, certificates and features, with same_date: how many share it), expired (what is already past; null when the station date is unknown) and a warning when the nearest expiry is 60 days away or fewer, or past, when a licence is not reported valid, or when an expiry could not be read as a date; note says what the reading could not do; {error} when the page was not read, saying which case it is (no permission, no such page, not HTML, not a licence page), never an empty licence. n4_license_info has the whole of it. drivers=true (default false; no extra request: it groups the rows of the networks, devices and points sections) adds drivers: per driver network {network (its slot path), name, type, status (its flags), enabled, devices, devices_bad, devices_bad_truncated, points, points_bad, points_bad_truncated}, and totals. devices counts the network's field devices (the local device left out) as total, down, fault, disabled (the disabled flag or enabled false) and unknown; points counts its proxy points (proxy extension not control:NullProxyExt; any other control point is no driver point and counts nowhere) as total, stale, fault, down, disabled and unknown. A status with several bits counts once in each of its categories, so the categories need not sum to total; unknown is a status the station did not answer as a number, never ok. devices_bad [{device, status, enabled false when so}] and points_bad [{point, status}] list the ones in any category, up to max_bad each (default 20), *_truncated true when cut. totals sums the networks and adds unassigned_points (proxy points under no network), proxy_unknown (points whose proxy type the station did not answer, not counted) and rows_truncated (a feeding query was cut: lower bounds). drivers is null with drivers_note when one of the three sections failed. device_detail=true (needs drivers=true, refused otherwise; two more requests at most, one BQL query over every device and one over every network, sent only when a network lists a bad device) adds to each devices_bad entry fault_cause, last_fail_cause, last_ok, last_fail (the device's faultCause and health.lastFailCause, health.lastOkTime, health.lastFailTime as the station writes them; a ping failure sets last_fail_cause and leaves fault_cause empty), address (from a known per-type slot: deviceAddress for Modbus devices, address network:mac for BACnet devices; null for any other type) and stale_points (its stale proxy points, from the points rows), and to each network port (its serialPortConfig.portName; null when it has none) and pattern: {kind bus, down, total, hint} when the network has 2 or more devices and all but at most one are down (at least 2 down: check bus wiring, termination, polarity and the port), {kind single, ...} when exactly one of 2 or more devices is bad and it is down (check that device's address and power), else null. A value the station did not give is null, never a guess; device_detail_note says which detail query failed. Without device_detail the drivers section is unchanged. platform=true (default false) adds platform: platform capacity and what is about to expire, each item null with a *_note saying why when it cannot be read, never a guess. heap {used_kb, committed_kb, max_kb, fraction, source}: used and committed are the JVM's totalMemory less freeMemory and totalMemory of the spy sysInfo page; max_kb is the sum of the defined maxima of the heap pools on spy util/JMX Info (null with max_note when it cannot be read), fraction is used_kb over max_kb. cpu {current, overall, cpus} and memory {total, free} repeat the system section (no request); the CPU usage slots hold -1 until the SystemService is polled, which its subscription by a load triggers, so the system section loads it once more when they are missing, and cpu is null with cpu_note (system.cpu_note too) when they stay unmeasured. history_db {histories, records, bytes, bytes_note, truncated, source}: the histories the spy localHistory page lists and their records summed; bytes is always null, no read-only page gives the size of the history files. licence {kind, name, expires, days_left, never_expires} is the license section's nearest expiry (no request); never_expires true when nothing on the licence page is dated. certificates lists the station's own key store certificates first ({alias, store station, expires, days_left, status}: one BOX load of Services/SecurityService/certificates, days_left the value of each entry's CertificateExpiryPoint and expires the station's date plus it), then the user and system trust store certificates of the spy securityInfo/Cryptography Info page ({alias, store, issued_by, expires, days_left}), each store nearest expiry first, up to 50, with certificates_count and certificates_note; null only when neither source answers. modules {count, truncated, items (only with include_modules), source} are the parts the spy module manager page lists. warnings lists a heap at 90% or more of its maximum, and the licence and each station or user certificate expired or expiring within expiry_warn_days (default 30) of the station's date; the system trust store (JDK roots) is one summary line, N system trust-store certificates expired or expiring (JDK roots; informational). Without platform the reply is unchanged.

base.description: Subtree ORD of the point, network and device counts, default station:|slot:/

device_detail.description: With drivers=true: add each bad device's fault cause, last fail cause, last ok and fail times, address and stale point count, and each network's port and bus or single-device pattern (two more requests at most)

drivers.description: Add drivers: devices and proxy points per driver network counted per down, fault, disabled and stale (no extra request)

expiry_warn_days.description: Window of the platform warnings: a licence or certificate expiring this many days away or fewer, or past, is warned about (with platform=true)

include_modules.description: List the loaded modules {name, vendor, version} in platform.modules (with platform=true; the count is always given)

max_bad.description: Cap of each network's devices_bad and points_bad lists (with drivers=true)

max_not_ok.description: Cap of the not-ok entries listed per section

platform.description: Add platform: heap, cpu, memory, history_db, licence, certificates and modules with expiry warnings (five more spy page reads and one BOX load)

timeout_s.description: HTTP timeout per request in seconds
